sources.title: Key-Gram: Extensible World Knowledge for Embodied Manipulation

omissions: Identity: the inspected title page identifies arXiv:2605.18556v1 [cs.RO], 18 May 2026. Title and all four authors match the catalog; no other revision was supplied or compared.
Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
That extraction limitation was addressed by inspecting all five figures, all eight tables, and every page supporting retained scientific details.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.
All five supplied text chunks were read completely, including references and appendices. Reference-only pages 11–12 were read as text but were not visually inspected.

synopsis: Key-Gram augments π0 and π0.5 with instruction-indexed embedding memory. A parser extracts reusable phrases; hashed lookup retrieves priors that modulate visual hidden states before attention. The backbone supplies future-visual representations and context for a separate action expert. Reported gains are strongest under distribution expansion and compositional manipulation, but the evidence does not isolate future prediction or establish lifelong, update-free knowledge retention.

problem.text: The authors argue that dense language–vision fusion makes sparse instruction tokens compete with visual tokens, while backbone adaptation can overwrite reusable task knowledge. They propose separating linguistic storage from online scene reasoning. Modality competition and interference are motivations, not directly measured causal effects here.

contributions.text: A conditional-memory module converts task phrases into deterministic multi-head lookups and injects their concatenated embeddings through token-wise gating, convolution, and residual addition.
Slot–head sub-tables offer modular capacity expansion and possible CPU placement. Experiments evaluate memory-augmented VLA policies on simulated benchmarks and physical dual-arm tasks.

inputs: Natural-language instruction I and initial visual observations V₀
External parser and layer-specific linguistic embedding tables
outputs: An action trajectory decoded by a separate action expert
A compact predicted future visual latent described in the architecture

steps.name: Extract reusable task phrases
steps.detail: A lightweight language model or API parser produces bounded-length key-grams, rather than contiguous n-grams. The RoboTwin prompt requests eight phrases of two to four words, with at least three action-bearing phrases. The parser model/version is unspecified.

steps.name: Address embedding memory
steps.detail: Word identifiers are zero-padded and hashed with deterministic odd multipliers and XOR. Each head retrieves an embedding; head and phrase outputs are concatenated. These are stored priors, not records of the robot's recent visual history.

steps.name: Fuse before attention
steps.detail: The concatenated memory is projected into a key and value. Incoming visual hidden states query the key through a scaled dot product and gate. A long-span convolution refines gated values before residual addition. Selected zero-based layers are (1, 8, 13).

steps.name: Produce two downstream predictions
steps.detail: Learnable queries cross-attend to final hidden states, followed by projection and two upsampling stages into VAE-compatible future latents. Separately, backbone KV cache conditions a smaller, architecturally isomorphic action expert that denoises trajectories by flow matching.

steps.name: Allocate memory by instruction regime
steps.detail: Simulation uses eight slots and four heads per slot; physical experiments use sixteen slots and two heads. Both use 32-dimensional head embeddings, 8,192 rows per table, 1,024 retrieved dimensions, and 8.39M embedding parameters per inserted layer. Convolution spans are eight and sixteen respectively.

training.text: Appendix A.5 explicitly reports full-parameter training. Statements that the backbone and expert are 'unchanged' describe preserved architecture and do not establish frozen weights. The source gives no complete loss formulation, visual/action loss weighting, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, or precise stage schedule.

Real-world data comprise 300 trajectories for each long-horizon task and two 50-trajectory expansion training sets. Sequential adaptation further trains on the second pairing before retesting the first.

inference.text: Parse the instruction, retrieve fixed-address entries, fuse them into visual computation, and decode actions from KV-conditioned denoising. The source describes CPU-resident memory as feasible because lookup is constant-time in total table size; it reports no end-to-end inference latency.

Figure 1 does not feed a decoded future image into the action expert; both pathways share backbone information. Action horizon, denoising step count, feedback frequency, and the deployed role of the future-visual output remain unspecified.

equations.explanation: Equation (1): aᵢ,ⱼ is a padded word identifier in key-gram i; M is maximum word length; ℓ and h index layer and hash head. The odd multipliers r are deterministic, ⊕ is bitwise XOR, and P is described as a prime table size. The resulting z addresses the embedding table.

Equation (4) and the following residual definition: H is the pre-attention hidden state, A the token-wise gate from Equation (3), and Vₘ the projected memory value. Gated memory is convolved and added before standard attention. The exact convolution layout is not specified.

results.setting: 50 tasks; Easy and Hard settings; 100 configurations with 100 trials each in unseen environments.
results.value: π0-KG: 80.3 Easy, 75.6 Hard; π0.5-KG: 89.0 Easy, 84.4 Hard.
results.interpretation: Reported 29.5%/9.9% relative gains are Hard-setting gains, not averages across both settings. Individual tasks can regress.

results.setting: Models trained on LIBERO; no target-domain fine-tuning for this column.
results.interpretation: Gains over corresponding backbones are 19.2 and 3.8 percentage points; reported relative gains are 35.8% and 4.5%.

results.setting: Separate in-domain fine-tuned columns, not the transfer protocol.
results.interpretation: Transfer gains coexist with a 0.2-point LIBERO decline for π0.5-KG; improvement is not universal.

results.setting: Piper dual-arm platform; picking, sorting, assembly.
results.interpretation: These are executed manipulation outcomes. The table reports relative mean gains of 15.4%/8.1%, without uncertainty estimates.

results.task: Physical compositional expansion and sequential adaptation
results.setting: Task 3: unseen Pen–Lighter; Task 4: unseen Charger–Matchbox car; Task 5: retest Pen–Charger after further training.
results.interpretation: The five-setting means are 81.6 versus 72.4 and 86.8 versus 80.0. One sequential retest cannot establish long-term forgetting resistance.

results.setting: π0.5; four named RoboTwin tasks; Easy:Hard weighted 1:9, then averaged across tasks.
results.comparison: Adding layer 13 after (1,8) gives 0.4 points at displayed precision.
results.interpretation: Early insertion carries most of this gain. Added layers also add parameters, so this is not a fixed-capacity isolation of gating or convolution.

limitations.text: The authors acknowledge evaluation on only π0 and π0.5, reliance on parser quality, and insufficient evidence across broader architectures or longer continual-learning settings.

No controlled future-head, parser, hash-capacity, or convolution ablation is reported. No quantitative future-latent metric establishes dynamics quality; gate activations alone do not prove reduced modality competition.

Source inconsistencies remain: the prose's near-0.1 vanilla gate floor differs from Figure 5's near-0.5 deep-layer markers. Table 1 reports 78.0 for π0-KG H=1 Hard, versus 77.9 in Table 6; ablation and appendix per-task rows also differ.

Equation (1) requires a prime modulus, whereas the configuration lists 8,192 rows. Their relationship is unexplained. Expansion by concatenation also changes fusion input width; the resizing and old-entry protection procedure is not specified.

reproduction.text: Reported compute is eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs, batch 16 per GPU/global 128, about 135 GB per GPU, roughly 128 samples/s, and 1–1.5 days per RoboTwin epoch. These are author-reported requirements, not measured here.

A faithful implementation needs parser/version and caching policy, word-ID mapping, hash seeds/moduli, memory initialization/update rules, convolution layout, backbone checkpoints, visual targets/losses, optimizer schedule, and control timing. Several are absent; real-world evaluation trial counts, random seeds, and uncertainty estimates are also unspecified.

Proposed checks should hold capacity constant while changing memory injection depth, and separately compare sequential retention with protected versus updateable memory. The illustrated edition specifies controls and falsifiable outcomes; neither check has been run.

reasoning.text: VLA and Dual-system are supported by the memory-guided backbone and separate KV-conditioned action expert. However, Section 3.4 explicitly describes future-visual and action prediction, so 'Not applicable' cannot mean no predictive world representation. Its training and inference contribution are insufficiently specified for a firm WAM quadrant assignment. Fine-tuning is documented, but a distinct data-augmentation contribution is not established. Preserve the catalog snapshot while flagging these qualifications.

discussionQuestions: Does the gain persist with parameter-matched late injection or instruction-independent memory?
Can old-task behavior be preserved when new key-gram slots change the fusion interface?
Does the future-visual branch improve executed control when its contribution is isolated?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title/author block and arXiv margin
evidence.detail: Exact title; Jingjing Fan, Siyuan Li, Botao Ren, Zhidong Deng; Tsinghua departments; arXiv:2605.18556v1, 18 May 2026. Fan and Li share equal contribution.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–2, Section 1
evidence.detail: Motivates functional separation of reusable linguistic knowledge from dynamic scene reasoning and claims reduced interference.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Figure 1 and caption; p. 4, Section 3.1
evidence.detail: Memory-guided VLM sends KV context to a distinct action expert; a separate VAE-compatible visual pathway is described. Key-Gram precedes attention.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 4–5, Section 3.2, Equations (1)–(2)
evidence.detail: Parser extraction, padded word IDs, odd-multiplier XOR hashing, prime modulus, embedding lookup and head concatenation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.3, Equations (3)–(4) and residual definition
evidence.detail: Concatenated memory projects to a key/value; visual queries provide token-wise gates; convolution precedes residual addition.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.4, Vision reasoning and Action inference
evidence.detail: Learnable visual queries, cross-attention and two upsampling stages; KV-conditioned, smaller isomorphic action expert uses flow-matching denoising.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Figure 2 and Section 3.5
evidence.detail: Slot–head physical tables form logical memory; expansion through slots, row capacity or parallel tables; device partitioning and CPU lookup are described.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 6–7, Section 4.1, Benchmarks and Model Configuration
evidence.detail: RoboTwin uses all 50 tasks, 100 clean/randomized configurations and 100 trials each; LIBERO uses four suites; transfer and target fine-tuning are separate protocols.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1, Real-world robot
evidence.detail: Piper platform; 300 trajectories per long-horizon task; two 50-trajectory pairing datasets; unseen pairings and sequential retesting protocol.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 1, Avg. 50 Tasks row, corresponding backbone/KG Easy and Hard columns
evidence.detail: π0 65.9/58.4 versus KG 80.3/75.6; π0.5 82.7/76.8 versus KG 89.0/84.4. Parentheses denote relative improvements.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 2, all rows and three protocol columns
evidence.detail: LIBERO, LIBERO-to-Plus transfer, and Plus fine-tuning values; includes π0.5-KG's 96.7 versus 96.9 LIBERO result.

evidence.detail: Long-horizon averages 69.3/82.0 for base models and 80.0/88.7 for KG; assembly 52/70 versus 66/82; selected physical rollouts.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Table 4, Tasks 1–5 and Avg.; Figure 4
evidence.detail: Expansion results distinguish familiar pairs, unseen recombinations and sequential adaptation. KG means 81.6/86.8 versus base 72.4/80.0.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 8–9, Section 4.4; p. 10, Table 5 and caption
evidence.detail: Four tasks: hanging mug, move stapler pad, pick dual bottles, stack blocks three. Easy:Hard 1:9 weighting; scores 51.0, 71.5, 76.8, 77.2.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Section 4.4, gate-probing paragraph; p. 10, Figure 5 and caption
evidence.detail: Colored/shaded curves encode score; red diamonds encode normalized gates on a separate axis. Vanilla deep-layer markers sit near 0.5 despite prose referring to a floor around 0.1; panel score axes differ.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 1, Avg. H=1 Hard; p. 10, Table 5; pp. 13–14, Table 6
evidence.detail: Table 6 reports 77.9 versus Table 1's 78.0 for π0-KG H=1 Hard. For π0.5-KG hanging mug Hard, Table 5 gives 35 versus Table 6's 36; tables are retained as distinct reports. Per-task regressions are present.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 14–15, Appendix A.2, introductory paragraph and extraction prompt
evidence.detail: RoboTwin parser prompt requests exactly eight phrases, two to four words each and at least three with action verbs. Some long PDF lines overflow the page.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 15–16, Appendix A.3 and Tables 7–8
evidence.detail: Simulation S=8,H=4; physical S=16,H=2; head width 32, memory width 1024, rows 8192, 32 tables and 8.39M embedding parameters per layer; spans 8/16; zero-based layers (1,8,13).

evidence.location: PDF p. 16, Appendix A.4
evidence.detail: Authors limit generality to two tested backbones, acknowledge external-parser dependence, and call for larger suites and longer continual-learning studies.

evidence.location: PDF p. 16, Appendix A.5
evidence.detail: Full-parameter training uses eight H200 GPUs; batch 16 per GPU/128 global, approximately 135 GB per GPU, 128 samples/s and 1–1.5 days per RoboTwin epoch.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 4–7, Sections 3–4.1; pp. 8–10, Sections 4.3–4.4; pp. 14–16, Appendices A.2–A.5
evidence.detail: Available method, experiment and configuration descriptions do not specify a complete training objective, visual loss/targets, optimizer schedule, parser identity or deployment timing; no dedicated future-prediction evaluation or component ablation beyond placement is reported.
